- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen subsequent forecast peaks by 5–15%.
- If sentiment is consistently low or negative, model overestimates recovery — shift forecast downward by 2–8% for next 3–5 periods.
- Model underestimates downward moves when sentiment is mildly negative — increase forecast lows by 3–7% to account for volatility.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model tends to overestimate mean reversion — adjust downward by 1–5% for early horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period sentiment-driven corrections — add a 1–3% downward bias in final 5–7 periods if sentiment turns negative.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive drops), model overestimates recovery — reduce forecast midpoints by 3–7%.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment when price is near support — if sentiment is negative and price is near recent low, add 2–5% downward buffer.
